title: Which terminal does my flight use? (T1, T2, T3)
body:
Delhi Airport has three passenger terminals: Terminal 1 (T1), Terminal 2 (T2) and Terminal 3 (T3), plus a cargo terminal and a general aviation terminal. Airlines are split between the terminals by flight-number series, so always check the terminal printed on your boarding pass or shown in your airline's message.

Allocation published by the airport (as of October 2026, effective 1 June 2026):
- Terminal 1: domestic flights of IndiGo (all series except 5000–5999), SpiceJet (all series except 8000–8999) and Akasa Air.
- Terminal 2: IndiGo flights in the 6E 2000 series, and Air India domestic flights numbered AI1700 to AI1899.
- Terminal 3: all international flights; IndiGo 5000–5999 series; SpiceJet 8000–8999 series; Air India Express; Alliance Air; and Air India domestic flights (the airport FAQ lists the AI1100–AI1199 series at T3).

The airport notes that allocations change from time to time, so recheck a day before you fly. You can see live flight information on the display screens (FIDS) inside and outside each terminal, on the flight information section of the airport website, or by calling the 24x7 airport call centre on +91-124-4797300 or +91-124-6838410. Your airline remains the final authority on terminal and gate.

If you go to the wrong terminal, use the free inter-terminal shuttle (see the article on moving between terminals). T2 and T3 are close enough to walk between using a dedicated pedestrian pathway.

title: Moving between terminals: free shuttle, walkway and buggy
body:
Delhi Airport runs a complimentary inter-terminal shuttle bus between Terminals 1, 2 and 3. As of October 2026 it runs about every 10 minutes.

Where to board:
- Terminal 3: inside the bus waiting lounge at the Arrival forecourt, near Pillar No. 10.
- Terminal 1: Arrival forecourt, towards the bus lanes.
- Terminal 2: the desk near VIP parking at Arrivals is listed as not operational; ask the information desk near the baggage belts for the current boarding point.

Who rides free: transfer passengers with a valid onward ticket get a complimentary coupon from the shuttle counter staff before boarding. Without a coupon, the bus staff collect a nominal fare.

T2 to T3 (and back): the two terminals are within walking distance on a dedicated pedestrian pathway. From T3 arrivals the path starts near Pillar No. 18; from T2 follow the signs to Terminal 3 after leaving the arrival hall. Senior citizens, expectant mothers, passengers with infants and passengers with reduced mobility can use a complimentary buggy between T2 and T3.

Other options: app cabs, prepaid taxis and the Metro feeder bus. Delhi Transport Corporation city buses also link T3, T2, T1 and ISBT Kashmere Gate.

Allow enough time. You must check in and clear security again at the departure terminal, so build the transfer into your connection time.

title: Connecting flights at DEL: international and domestic transfers
body:
How you connect depends on where you arrive and where you depart from. All international flights use Terminal 3.

International to international: the whole transfer happens inside T3. Follow the orange transfer signs to the international transfer area, where your airline's counter helps with formalities, then clear security and go up to departures. If you already hold your onward boarding pass, your bag is normally transferred automatically; check the final destination printed on your bag tag. Without an onward boarding pass, or if your bag is not tagged to the final destination, you clear immigration and customs at Delhi and check in again. Check whether you need a transit visa before travelling.

International to domestic: you clear immigration, collect your bags and clear customs at T3. If your domestic flight is also from T3, follow the yellow domestic transfer signs and do not exit the building. If your onward flight is from T1 or T2, exit the terminal and take the free inter-terminal shuttle or a cab, enter the departure level and check in again.

Domestic to domestic: if your bag is tagged to the final destination it moves automatically. Follow the yellow signs, clear security and go to your gate. If not, collect your bag first and re-check it in. At T2, onward T2 passengers with a boarding pass can use the internal transfer area, but there is no baggage re-check facility there and only one handbag is allowed.

Domestic to international: go to T3, check in, clear immigration and security again.

title: When to reach the airport, check-in times and self-service options
body:
Recommended arrival time (as of October 2026): the airport's general FAQ asks passengers to reach 3 hours before domestic departures and 4 hours before international departures. Its check-in guide gives a minimum of 2 hours for domestic and 3 hours for international flights. During peak or fog season, use the longer figures.

Check-in counters open 3 hours before scheduled departure for domestic flights and 4 hours before for international flights. Airline counter closing times vary by airline, so check your ticket.

Entering the terminal: only ticketed passengers may enter. Show a valid government photo ID and a printed or digital boarding pass or ticket at the entry gate.

Web check-in: most airlines open web check-in from 48 hours to 1 hour before departure. Download or print your boarding pass.

Kiosks: self check-in (CUSS) kiosks at T1, T2 and T3 print boarding passes and bag tags, up to 1 hour before departure.

Drop-n-Fly (self baggage drop): print the bag tag at a kiosk, attach it, scan your boarding pass, declare the bag has no prohibited or dangerous items, and load it onto the belt. The airport says this saves about 15–20 minutes. It is available at the T3 check-in hall (Row P, near Gate 7) and the T1 check-in hall for domestic flights and some international flights at T3. T2 has 4 self baggage drop points in check-in rows C and D. Airport staff help at the machines if there is an error.

title: DigiYatra: face-based entry and boarding
body:
DigiYatra is a Ministry of Civil Aviation initiative run with the DigiYatra Foundation. It uses facial recognition so your face works as your boarding pass at airport entry, security check and the boarding gate. The airport says processing takes under 3 seconds at each point.

Who can use it: domestic passengers departing from T1, T2 or T3. It is not yet available for international departures.

How to register:
1. Install the DigiYatra app from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store.
2. Sign up with your mobile number and OTP. The number must be linked to your Aadhaar.
3. Link your Aadhaar through DigiLocker or directly with your Aadhaar number. DigiLocker is not mandatory.
4. Take a selfie, validate it against Aadhaar and save.
5. Do web check-in with your airline and upload or scan the boarding pass in the app before your flight.

The name on Aadhaar must match the name on your boarding pass. You can upload a boarding pass booked from a different mobile number. Always carry a printed or mobile boarding pass as backup.

DigiYatra e-gates (as of October 2026):
- Terminal 1: gates 1D, 2D, 3D, 4D, 5D and 6D.
- Terminal 2: gates 1B, 2B, 3B, 4B and 5B.
- Terminal 3: gates 1B, 2A and 2B.

At the security e-gate, look into the camera for validation, then proceed for screening and boarding. For help, call the airport's DigiYatra helpline on 0124-4797311 or 0124-6838400.

title: Security screening, liquids rule and cabin bag tips
body:
International passengers clear immigration first and then security. Domestic passengers go to security after check-in.

At the screening point:
- Put metal objects, belts, bracelets and jackets in the blue trays.
- Put phones, laptops, tablets, smartwatches and fitness trackers in a separate blue tray. Keep small loose items such as chargers, headphones and glasses inside a tray or case.
- If you are asked to remove your shoes, use the red trays.
- Food and normal photographic film are safe to pass through the X-ray.

Liquids, aerosols and gels (LAGs) in hand baggage: each container can hold at most 100 ml, even if it is only partly full. All containers must fit in one transparent, resealable plastic bag of no more than 1 litre. Free bags are available at the start of the security queue. Essential medicines and baby food are exceptions, but carry a doctor's prescription for medicines.

Cabin bags: under airline rules and government guidelines, you may carry only one handbag or cabin bag on board. The size and weight limit is set by your airline and printed on your ticket.

Not allowed in hand baggage: nail cutters with a knife, scissors, Swiss knives and similar sharp items, and spare batteries beyond the permitted limits. Do not pack power banks, lighters or e-cigarettes in checked baggage.

If you have a pacemaker, prosthetic limb, other medical device or a battery-powered wheelchair, tell the security staff before screening.

title: Prohibited and restricted items (BCAS list)
body:
The Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) publishes the list of items passengers may not carry. Delhi Airport hosts this list and points to bcasindia.gov.in for the full version. The examples below are paraphrased from the BCAS annexures (as of October 2026).

Not allowed in cabin or checked baggage (examples): e-cigarettes and all electronic nicotine devices, including heat-not-burn and e-hookah; lighters and lighter fluid; safety matches; fireworks and party poppers; fuels, gasoline and gas torches; spray paint, turpentine and paint thinner; liquid bleach; camphor; copra (dried coconut); compressed gas cylinders; mace, pepper spray and tear gas; hoverboards and Segways; satellite phones such as Thuraya or Iridium unless the Department of Telecommunications has given permission; and spillable batteries.

Checked baggage only (examples): knives (except round-bladed butter knives and plastic cutlery), box cutters, hammers, drills, axes, crowbars, corkscrews, knitting needles, footballs, golf balls and other inflatable or hard balls (deflated), powdered spices including chilli, coconut, tapes, and drones (without batteries).

Cabin only: spare and loose lithium batteries and power banks. Lithium-ion batteries can be up to 100 Wh each, and each person can carry at most 2 spares.

Alcohol: retail-packed drinks with 24%–70% alcohol go in checked baggage, up to 5 litres per person. On domestic flights liquor goes only in checked baggage, sealed. Duty-free liquor bought after security on an international departure, or carried by an international arrival connecting to a domestic flight, must stay in a STEB (security tamper-evident bag). Ghee or cooking oil can go in checked baggage up to 5 kg/litres per passenger, or in the cabin within the liquids rule.

Firearms travel only in checked baggage, by licence holders and with airline approval. Items confiscated at security are not deposited with Lost & Found.

title: Baggage allowance, excess baggage and wrapping
body:
Your baggage allowance is set by your airline, not by the airport. Free check-in weight and the cabin bag size and weight differ by airline, route and fare type, and are printed on your ticket or booking confirmation. Check them before packing.

Cabin baggage: one handbag or cabin bag per passenger, under airline and government rules.

Excess baggage: if you go over your airline's limit, you pay excess charges at the airline counter. The airport notes that buying extra allowance in advance from your airline is usually cheaper than paying at the airport.

Other baggage services at Delhi Airport (as of October 2026):
- Excess baggage shipping: Avaan, the airport's authorised concessionaire, ships extra baggage across India and worldwide. The airport says this can save up to 3 times compared with excess fees.
- Baggage wrapping using biodegradable material.
- Left luggage: available at T3 in the Airport Metro building.
- Porter service for heavy bags.

Packing tips: pack fragile items securely and tell airline staff. Keep passports, boarding passes and medicines in your hand baggage. Do not put power banks, spare lithium batteries, lighters or e-cigarettes in checked bags.

Pets: some airlines allow small pets in the cabin and others only as cargo. Confirm with your airline in advance.

If your checked bag is missing or damaged when you land, see the article on delayed, lost or damaged baggage (PIR).

title: Delayed, lost or damaged baggage: filing a PIR and claiming
body:
Checked baggage is the airline's responsibility. If your bag does not arrive on the belt or comes out damaged, deal with your airline before you leave the baggage hall.

1. Go to your airline's baggage services desk in the arrival hall.
2. File a Property Irregularity Report (PIR). Give your bag tag stub, boarding pass, a description of the bag and its contents, and your delivery address and phone number.
3. Keep the PIR reference number, for example DELAI12345. You need it to track the bag and to claim. A PIR on its own is not a claim.
4. Send a written claim to the airline with a copy of the PIR and your receipts. Under the Montreal Convention time limits that airlines apply:
   - Damaged bags: within 7 days of receiving the bag.
   - Delayed bags: within 21 days of receiving the bag.
   - A bag not traced within 21 days is normally treated as lost.
5. Keep receipts for essential items you buy while waiting. Airlines may consider reimbursing them under their conditions of carriage.

Liability limits in the Ministry of Civil Aviation Passenger Charter (2019 edition): for domestic travel, the airline's liability for loss, delay or damage to baggage is limited to ₹20,000 per passenger. For international travel, the charter gives 1,131 SDR per passenger. International limits are periodically revised, so ask your airline for the figure that currently applies.

On this help desk, signed-in passengers can ask for the status of a PIR by reference number. If the airline does not resolve your claim, you can escalate on the AirSewa portal or app.

title: Your rights if your flight is delayed
body:
Indian airlines must look after passengers during long delays under DGCA Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) Section 3, Series M, Part IV. The Ministry of Civil Aviation's Passenger Charter summarises these rights as follows.

1. Meals and refreshments. You have checked in on time and the airline expects a delay of:
- 2 hours or more for flights with a block time of up to 2½ hours;
- 3 hours or more for flights with a block time of over 2½ hours and up to 5 hours; or
- 4 hours or more for all other flights.
The airline must then give you free meals and refreshments in line with the waiting time.

2. Domestic flight delayed by more than 6 hours: the airline should tell you the new time more than 24 hours before the original departure. It must also offer either an alternate flight within 6 hours or a full refund.

3. Free hotel stay: the airline must provide free hotel accommodation if the delay is more than 24 hours. The same applies if your flight was scheduled between 20:00 and 03:00 and is delayed by more than 6 hours.

Block time is the time from pushback at the departure gate to arrival at the destination gate.

What the airport does: Delhi Airport shows live status on its display screens and website, but airlines decide on rebooking, refunds, meals and hotels. Speak to your airline's counter or call centre. On this help desk you can ask for the live status of any flight by flight number and date.

In fog season (mid-December to February), check your flight status before leaving home.

title: Flight cancelled: alternate flight, refund and compensation
body:
Under the DGCA rules summarised in the Ministry of Civil Aviation Passenger Charter, airlines must tell you about a cancellation at least two weeks before departure. They must then arrange an alternate flight or a refund, whichever you accept.

Informed less than two weeks before, but at least 24 hours before departure: the airline must offer an alternate flight departing within 2 hours of your original time, or a refund, whichever you accept.

Not informed as above, or you missed a connection booked on the same ticket: the airline must give you an alternate flight you accept, or pay compensation in addition to a full refund:
- block time up to 1 hour: ₹5,000 or the booked one-way basic fare plus airline fuel charge, whichever is less;
- block time over 1 hour and up to 2 hours: ₹7,500 or the one-way basic fare plus fuel charge, whichever is less;
- block time over 2 hours: ₹10,000 or the one-way basic fare plus fuel charge, whichever is less.

Also:
- If you have already reported for the flight, the airline must give you free meals and refreshments while you wait for the alternate flight.
- You must give adequate contact details when booking. If you don't, no financial compensation is payable.
- If the airline moves you to a different airport or terminal, it bears the cost of the transfer. If you were told at least 6 hours in advance, you arrange your own transport.

No compensation is owed for extraordinary circumstances (force majeure) beyond the airline's control, such as weather, air traffic control decisions, security risks, natural disasters or strikes. Delays caused by fog at Delhi usually fall in this category.

title: Denied boarding, refunds and the 24-hour free cancellation
body:
Denied boarding due to overbooking: an airline must first ask for volunteers to give up their seats. If you are denied boarding against your will after reporting on time with a confirmed booking, the Passenger Charter sets out the following.
- If the airline arranges an alternate flight departing within 1 hour of the original time, no compensation is due.
- Alternate flight within 24 hours: 200% of the booked one-way basic fare plus airline fuel charge, up to a maximum of ₹10,000.
- Alternate flight more than 24 hours later: 400% of the same amount, up to ₹20,000.
- If you do not take an alternate flight: a full refund plus 400% of the same amount, up to ₹20,000.

Refund timelines: immediate if you paid in cash at an airline office; within 7 days if you paid by credit card; through the travel agent if you booked through one.

When you cancel a ticket, the airline must refund all statutory taxes and user fees, such as the user development fee, airport development fee and passenger service fee, even on non-refundable fares. Keeping the money as a credit shell is your choice, not the default. You cannot be charged extra just to process a refund.

The 24-hour free cancellation or change: within 24 hours of booking, you can cancel or change a ticket without extra charges. This applies if the first flight departs at least 7 days after booking. Correcting a name within 24 hours of booking is also free.

Escalation: raise the complaint with the airline's help desk first. If you are not satisfied, file a grievance on the AirSewa app or portal, and after that with a consumer forum or court.

title: Lost something at the airport? How Lost & Found works
body:
Items found inside the terminals and around them go to the Lost Property office of that terminal within 24 hours and are entered in the airport's lost property database. The service is free. Anyone asking for a fee on Delhi Airport's behalf, or offering to courier items, is not authorised. The airport does not provide a courier service.

Lost something on the aircraft? Contact your airline. Items left on board are handled by the airline.

How to report or search:
- Search the database on the airport website, or file a report through the Lost & Found report form.
- Email lostproperty.dial@gmrgroup.in.
- Lost less than 7 days ago: call the terminal desk (24x7). T2 and T3: 9958098651. T1: 9650495769.
- Lost more than 7 days ago: call the Lost Property Main Office on 011-42489617 or 011-42489616. It is at Terminal 2, Departure Level, near Gate No. 1. Hours are 09:30–18:00, Monday to Saturday; it is closed on the 2nd, 4th and 5th Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.

To collect, bring proof of travel (a boarding card or passport stamp), a government photo ID and a detailed description of the item. Someone collecting on your behalf needs their own photo ID and your signed authorisation letter. A PAN card copy may be requested to verify your signature.

How long items are kept (as of October 2026): collect from the terminal within 7 days. For collection outside office hours, email at least 48 hours ahead. Most items, including phones, laptops, jewellery, passports and liquor, are kept for 30 days. Voter ID, driving licence and other photo IDs are kept for 5 days. Low-value items such as belts, bottles, umbrellas, books, keys and cables are kept for 7 days. Credit and debit cards are destroyed immediately. Items removed by CISF at security are not kept by Lost & Found.

title: Parking at T1, T2 and T3: rates and where to park
body:
Parking is open 24x7 at all three terminals, with CCTV and patrolling, and has dedicated spaces for passengers with reduced mobility.

Car parking rates per visit (as of October 2026; tariff effective 15 April 2025), private car / commercial car, in ₹:
- Up to 30 minutes: 160 / 270
- 30 minutes to 1 hour: 250 / 400
- 1 to 2 hours: 320 / 500
- 2 to 3 hours: 400 / 600
- 3 to 4 hours: 500 / 700
- 4 to 24 hours: 600 / 800
- Lost ticket: 600 / 700
At T3 the first 12 minutes are free.

Two-wheelers (T1 and T2): ₹40 for up to 30 minutes, ₹80 for 30 minutes to 2 hours, then ₹40 for each extra hour up to 8 hours, and ₹400 from 8 to 24 hours. A lost ticket costs ₹400.

Where to park:
- T3: Multi-Level Car Parking (MLCP) opposite the terminal. It has air-conditioned waiting lounges, food outlets, baby care rooms and washrooms. Non-FASTag cars use Private Entry Lane No. 5. Validate your ticket at the pay booth before you exit.
- T2: at departures, take the extreme left lane before the departure ramp. From arrivals, the T2 car park is just after the first tunnel on the T3 walkway.
- T1: the car park is about 2 minutes' walk from the arrival forecourt. Park & Fly and Long Stay zones are available for self-drive flyers.

Parking helpline: T2 and T3 +91-8800493889; T1 +91-8800493897.

Rates are revised from time to time. Check the tariff board at the entry.

title: Park & Fly: pre-booked long-stay parking
body:
Park & Fly lets you pre-book a parking space at Delhi Airport while you travel. Pre-booking guarantees your space.

Where:
- Terminal 3: the Park N Fly / Long Stay Zone on Level 2 of the Multi-Level Car Parking (MLCP) opposite the terminal.
- Terminal 1: the marked Park N Fly / Long Stay zones.

Booking rules (as of October 2026):
- Validity: a booking covers 24 hours from the check-in time in your booking.
- Cancellation: allowed only at least 12 hours before the scheduled check-in time.
- Documents: usually only your name and mobile number, checked at the counter.
- Overstay: if you stay beyond the booked period, you pay the difference at the pay booth when you exit.
- At T3, non-FASTag cars enter through Private Entry Lane No. 5. Validate your ticket or payment at the pay booth before driving to the exit.

The Park & Fly tariff follows the published parking rates (private car / commercial car, ₹): up to 30 minutes 160 / 270; 30 minutes to 1 hour 250 / 400; 1–2 hours 320 / 500; 2–3 hours 400 / 600; 3–4 hours 500 / 700. The tariff has been in effect since 15 April 2025.

Support (24x7): T3 +91-8800493889, T1 +91-8800493897.

Signed-in customers on this help desk can check a Park & Fly booking by its reference number, including the slot, check-in and check-out times and the amount paid.

title: Wheelchair and special assistance (PRM)
body:
Passengers with reduced mobility (PRM) include elderly passengers, pregnant women, people travelling with infants and people with physical disabilities.

Wheelchairs are the airline's responsibility. Request one when you book your ticket and remind your airline before leaving for the airport. The airport's Hoi app lets you contact airline wheelchair support directly. Under the Passenger Charter you should tell the airline about your needs at least 48 hours before departure.

At the airport:
- Drop-off: at T3, Lane 1 of the departure forecourt (opposite Gate 3) is for UDID or Divyang card holders. Other PRM passengers can be dropped at any lane opposite Gates 3 and 6.
- Dedicated entry: all gates at T1, Gate 4 at T2 (Gate 4B is the PRM gate, with a PRM desk between Gates 4 and 5), and Gates 3 and 6 at T3.
- Dedicated security lanes: all zones at T1, Zone 2 at T2 and Zone 0 at T3.
- PRM phones at T2 departures connect straight to the airlines for wheelchair requests.
- Parking: dedicated PRM bays in the first row at T1 and on Levels 1 and 2 of the T3 MLCP near pillars A3–A4.
- PRM-friendly washrooms with call buttons, buggies at pier junctions, lifts with Braille keys and the Hidden Disability Sunflower programme.
- On arrival, dedicated immigration counters are available.

Paid wheelchair help is offered by the airport's partners (Aroon Aviation and Avia Xpert) for anyone who prefers not to walk long distances.

Your rights under the Passenger Charter: an airline cannot refuse to carry you with your assistive aids, escort or guide dog. A refusal must be explained in writing. You do not need a medical certificate to travel without an escort.

title: Lounges, transit hotel and other terminal facilities
body:
Lounges: Encalm runs the lounges in all three terminals. Card-based access is free or low-cost with many credit and debit cards, so check with your bank. You can also pay at the entrance. Walk-in prices excluding tax (as of October 2026):
- Domestic departure and arrival lounges: ₹1,796 for up to 2 hours, then ₹593 per extra hour. Children aged 6–11: ₹1,355.
- International departure lounges: ₹2,898 for up to 2 hours, then ₹1,296 per extra hour. Children aged 6–11: ₹1,864.
Pets are not allowed in lounges. Present your boarding pass on entry.

T3 also has transit lounges with nap and shower facilities in the arrivals area: domestic opposite exit gate 1, international opposite exit gate 6. Encalm Prive (business class style) is on Level 3 of International Departures.

Staying over: the Holiday Inn Express transit hotel is inside the T3 building, and Aerocity's hotels are within 2 km. At T3, passengers with a ticket for travel within the next 24 hours can use the waiting area in the Airport Metro building, which is connected by skywalk. T1 has no waiting room.

Other facilities:
- Medanta medical centres run 24x7 at T1, T2 and T3, with ambulances on call.
- Child care lounges are available at all terminals.
- Free Wi-Fi requires a working phone number for the OTP.
- Money exchange counters are at T3 arrivals and departures.
- Smoking zones are inside the terminals after security only.
- Atithya meet-and-assist (by Encalm) can be booked on +91-9289366950. Infants under 2 go free.

title: Customs on arrival: duty-free allowance and what to declare
body:
After immigration and baggage collection, all international arrivals pass through customs. Use the Green Channel if you have nothing dutiable or prohibited. Use the Red Channel if you do. Walking through the Green Channel with dutiable or prohibited goods can lead to confiscation, a penalty or prosecution. Smuggling gold can lead to arrest. You can also file your declaration before you fly using the ATITHI app.

Duty-free allowance under the Baggage Rules, 2026, in force from 2 February 2026 (as of October 2026), for arrivals by air or sea:
- Residents, tourists of Indian origin and foreigners on a non-tourist visa: goods up to ₹75,000.
- Foreign tourists: goods up to ₹25,000.
- Used personal effects are duty-free in addition.
- Passengers aged 18 or over may also bring one new laptop or notepad duty-free on top of the allowance.
The allowance is per person and does not cover firearms, more than 50 cartridges, gold or silver other than ornaments, or televisions.

Alcohol and tobacco within the allowance: up to 2 litres of liquor or wine, and up to 100 cigarettes, 25 cigars or 125 g of tobacco.

Jewellery: residents and tourists of Indian origin who have lived abroad for more than one year may bring jewellery duty-free: up to 40 g for women and 20 g for other passengers.

Currency: declare foreign currency notes above US$5,000, or total foreign exchange (notes plus traveller's cheques) above US$10,000. Residents may carry Indian currency up to ₹25,000.

Goods above the allowance attract customs duty. Ask the customs officer at the Red Channel for the applicable rate.

title: Immigration at DEL: departing and arriving internationally
body:
All international flights operate from Terminal 3.

Departing: enter T3, check in with your airline, then clear immigration, then security. Have your valid passport, visa (if required) and boarding pass ready. The immigration officer checks your documents, may ask about your travel plans, and clears you. Customs declarations on departure are usually needed only if you carry high-value items such as jewellery, large amounts of foreign currency or electronics, or goods subject to export restrictions. In that case, visit the Customs Declaration counter. Some passengers are randomly selected for customs checks, and the airline tells you at check-in.

Fast Track Immigration – Trusted Traveller Programme (FTI-TTP): Indian nationals and OCI cardholders who are pre-verified under the programme can use dedicated fast-track counters on departure and arrival.

Arriving:
- Indian passport holders use the Indian Passport Holder counters.
- Foreign nationals fill in the disembarkation form, which is given on board or available at the arrival pier junction, and use the Foreign Passport Holder counters. First-time foreign visitors register their biometrics (face and fingerprints) at the kiosks on the arrival piers before immigration.
- OCI and PIO cardholders follow the foreign-national process and use their dedicated counters.
- For e-Visa or visa on arrival rules, see the Bureau of Immigration website (boi.gov.in).

After immigration, check the display screens for your baggage belt, collect your bags and go through customs.

Satellite phones may not be carried when travelling to India unless permitted by the government.

title: Travelling in fog season (December to February)
body:
Dense fog is common in Delhi from mid-December to February and can disrupt flights.

What the airport has: CAT IIIB instrument landing systems on Runways 11, 29 and 28. These guide aircraft to land in very low visibility, but only if the aircraft is CAT IIIB equipped and the pilot is CAT IIIB trained. Airlines are expected to roster trained pilots during fog.

Visibility limits: aircraft can land with a runway visual range (RVR) down to 50 metres. Take-off normally needs an RVR above 125 metres, or above 75 metres for aircraft with an approved lateral guidance system. This is why arrivals sometimes continue while departures wait.

Why flights are delayed or cancelled: one late aircraft knocks on across the airline's network. Weather at the destination matters too. Safety comes first, and airlines may combine flights or swap aircraft.

What you should do:
- Check your flight status with your airline, or on this help desk, before you leave home.
- If you are asked to check in and wait, do so. Fog can lift suddenly and flights then move quickly.
- Food outlets, shops, and rest and shower facilities at T3 are available while you wait.
- For a cancellation, your airline offers rebooking, a refund or other options under its policy and the DGCA rules. Weather-related disruption usually counts as an extraordinary circumstance, so cash compensation may not apply. Your right to meals and refreshments during long delays still applies.
